title: Sparse innervation, big consequences
objective: Connect sparse visceral innervation to the lab's approach to gut and pancreas afferents.

steps.title: Few neurons, whole organ
steps.body: Compared with skin, an organ like the **[[colon]]** or pancreas is innervated by relatively few [[DRG]] afferents, each covering a lot of tissue. That sparseness is why visceral sensation is diffuse — and why mapping *which* neurons do what is both hard and valuable.

steps.prompt: Why is identifying visceral afferent subtypes especially important?
options: With so few afferents, each subtype's role is outsized
Each organ is served by one uniform afferent type
Skin afferent classes map directly onto visceral ones
Visceral subtypes are already fully catalogued
steps.explanation: With sparse innervation, a handful of molecularly-defined subtypes can carry distinct jobs — so defining and manipulating them (Cre lines, DREADDs) is how you learn what each does.

variants.setup: An organ is covered by only a few afferent subtypes.
variants.prompt: How valuable is identifying each subtype?
options: Very — each likely has a distinct role
Low — a few subtypes can't differ much
variants.reveal: Few subtypes means each is likely specialized, so identifying them is high-value.

steps.setup: You want to know what one colon afferent subtype does to sensation and motility.
steps.prompt: Which strategy fits the lab's toolkit?
options: Target that subtype with a Cre line, then silence it with a DREADD
Silence every DRG neuron at once with a pan-neuronal DREADD
Image that subtype's calcium activity without ever manipulating it
steps.reveal: A subtype-specific **[[Cre]]** line plus a silencing **[[DREADD]]** isolates one population's contribution — the colon paper's playbook, and the template for your pancreas project.

variants.prompt: To test one visceral subtype's function, the lab would…
options: Target it genetically, then silence it with a DREADD
Silence every DRG neuron at once with a DREADD
Record its activity without manipulating it
variants.explanation: Genetic targeting + DREADD silencing isolates one subtype's role.

steps.title: The through-line
steps.body: Sparse visceral innervation is the reason the field is only now mapping these neurons — and why the lab's genetic, subtype-level approach (Tracks C and E) is the way in.

sources.note: DRG afferents sensing distal-colon mechanics; visceral stretch sensation.
